title: Keeping Grocery Prices Affordable for Singaporeans Given Rising Prices in Global Commodity Markets
what_it_is: Keeping Grocery Prices Affordable for Singaporeans Given Rising Prices in Global Commodity Markets

sections.label: Food import diversification and assistance
sections.summary: Singapore, affected by rising commodity prices, has diversified food import sources and given targeted assistance to lower income households, importing food from over 170 countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As a small and open economy that imports our essential food supplies, Singapore has been affected by these developments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To reduce the impact of rising commodity prices on groceries, we have diversified our food import sources and also provided targeted assistance to lower income households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Today, we import food from more than 170 countries.

sections.label: Coping with daily necessity prices
sections.summary: The Government works with cooperatives on price freezes and MSF provides ComCare Assistance, while volatility in food and essential product prices is likely to continue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To help Singaporeans cope with the increase in prices in daily necessities, the Government continues to work with cooperatives, such NTUC FairPrice, on Community Support programmes, such as the price freeze on essential items under their house brand during the period March 2019 to December 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For low-income and vulnerable families, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) continues to provide ComCare Assistance to support their daily living expenses, such as food, clothing, transportation and communications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: MSF regularly reviews the ComCare schemes to ensure that the assistance given takes into account changes in the prices of essential items and feedback from stakeholders who work closely with the low-income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will always do our best to protect our supply of essential food commodities and keep prices stable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: However, these are extraordinary times and it is likely that we will continue to see volatility in the prices of food supplies and essential products due to global uncertainties, such as delays in transportation due to border controls and shortage of shipping capacity.
